chapter: Louis Armstrong picture, Kid Rena record and Bunk
title: Recording the sides, takes and what the record sold
summary: Each side took about forty minutes and one take was spoiled. Rene says the producer made money while the record's local sales were modest.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Huh? Yeah, it didn't take, it took, no, it took a little, about an hour, an hour and then, where we, it didn't take over, it's five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty, twenty, twenty, thirty, thirty, thirty, forty, forty minutes. Each, each one of them, take about forty minutes, we all, we, they had three, it was a three-minute record, that's all it was, three minutes.
You could make eight times in a hurry that way.

Well you see the way it is, you see, we, had everything down perfect. The fella gave us a little ideas and everything, and we went right on by it. Every time we cut, we didn't make no mistake. I think we made one, one blunder, one blunder, we, we, we really forgot to catch the sign. And that, that spoiled the record, you see. The record had to go, three minutes I think, or two minutes and a half, but I think it was three minutes, right, you think, or two and a half, I didn't time them. But he fella had to time.
Well did that guy tell you how to play that man from New York right here?

Well, no, he, cause he was, you know, we, you know how it is, you know, bro, okay. He couldn't, all we could see, he couldn't hear nothing, you know. All the people standing on our side could hear. All he just wanted was to do was to play, you see, cut the record. And every time we cut the record, then he, we waited a little while, then he played over, see, then he'd do this. When he got ready to bed, he said, well, now we're gonna fix you up, say, this is, we got something good there. And we boys, we get the garage, he said, boop, he went on across the seat. That guy must have been a million dollars across there. He said, he come right on straight to London, boy, what? Have your social record over there. Yeah, my wife went to take the case off, I said, no.
I don't think he made much money off of them. I think they made more than that money back. I don't think he made a million dollars.

Well, I'll tell you, from what I can understand, he made plenty of money. But it kept on a secret, but he made plenty of money. When he first went there, when he first went with that record, then people were involved in the record. He sold plenty. I didn't do too much, you see, because people was used to that band, you know. And then they had other bands that come up, then the big bands began to come up, you see. And the people got a lack of, and all they heard about Ray's band and all that. Just like you used to, you know, the band, you make the record.
